title: Default address fallback
statement_markdown: Return each customer name and preferred address. Use shipping_address when present, otherwise billing_address, otherwise 'No address'. Sort by name.

examples.output: [["Alice","123 Ship St"],["Bob","789 Bill St"],["Charlie","No address"],["David","321 Ship St"]]
examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

hints: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL expression.
Place shipping, billing, and the fallback text in priority order.
explanation: COALESCE checks its arguments from left to right and stops at the first non-NULL value. It models fallback rules without several CASE branches. A common mistake is comparing NULL with = instead of using NULL-aware functions. CASE is an alternative when fallback rules require conditions beyond NULL.
reference_solution: SELECT name, COALESCE(shipping_address, billing_address, 'No address') AS address FROM customers ORDER BY name

validation.setup_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR(50), shipping_address VARCHAR(100), billing_address VARCHAR(100)); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', '123 Ship St', '456 Bill St'), (2, 'Bob', NULL, '789 Bill St'), (3, 'Charlie', NULL, NULL), (4, 'David', '321 Ship St', NULL);
